body.p: Claims 1 to 20 are currently pending in the application, with claims 1-4 having been examined and claims 5-20 previously withdrawn. In this Reply, claim 1 has been amended for clarity, claim 2 has been cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer, and claim 21 has been added. The amendments are fully supported by the specification and figures of the present application as originally filed, and do not add new matter. For example, support for the amendments can be found at least on paras. [0011], [0013], [0026], and [0027] of the specification as originally filed. Favorable reconsideration of the present application is respectfully requested in light of the amendments herein and the following comments.
I. Claims 1-4 recite eligible subject matter under 35 U.S.C. § 101

The Office Action asserts that claims 1-4 are directed to an abstract idea and rejects those claims under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to the abstract idea. This rejection of claim 2 is now moot in view of the cancellation of that claim. This rejection is traversed. Reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection are respectfully requested for at least the following reasons.
The claims as currently presented recite patent eligible subject matter and, thus, render this rejection moot.

Further, the Office Action assesses the patent eligibility of claims 1 to 4 collectively, without providing a claim-by-claim assessment of patent eligibility. Thus, the Office Action fails to comply with examination procedure as stipulated in MPEP § 2106.05:

Examiners should examine each claim for eligibility separately, based on the particular elements recited therein. Claims should not be judged to automatically stand or fall with similar claims in an application. For instance, one claim may be ineligible because it is directed to a judicial exception without amounting to significantly more, but another claim dependent on the first may be eligible because it recites additional elements that do amount to significantly more. (Emphasis
added.)

Consequently, the Office Action unequivocally conveys that dependent claims 3 and 4 automatically fall with independent claim 1. Accordingly, at the very least, this rejection of claims 1, 3, and 4 is improper and should be removed.

In sum, it is clear that claims 1, 3, and 4 satisfy the patent eligibility requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 101. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of those claims under Section 101.
II. Claims 1-4 are definite within the bounds of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b)
Claims 1-4 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). The amendments put forth herein render this rejection moot. Accordingly, Applicant requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
III. New claim 21
Claim 21 has been added in this Reply. Claim 21 depends from claim 1 and includes allowable subject matter.
IV. Conclusion

Each issue raised in the Office Action has been addressed in this Reply. Therefore, the present application is in condition for allowance. Applicant thus respectfully requests prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance.

If for any reason the Examiner feels the application is not now in condition for allowance it is respectfully requested that they contact, by telephone, the undersigned practitioner at the indicated telephone number to arrange for an interview to expedite the disposition of this case.

Other than any fees submitted herewith, Applicant believes no further fees are owed. However, if a fee is due, please charge our Deposit Account Number 01-2300, under number 043505.00470 from which the undersigned is authorized to draw.
